text:
alex_support: Heads-up — customer AcmeCorp reported a sudden p95/p99 latency regression on tool-calls yesterday after the 22:00 deploy. They see p95 jump from ~240ms to 1.2s and p99 to 2.8s for endpoints that route to the tool router.

maria_eng-runtime: Ack. Any correlation with model changes or new schema validations?

alex_support: They said it only happens on requests that include function/tool calling + structured JSON output. Regular chat generation looks fine. They provided a short repro and logs.

kevin_oncall: Can you paste the logs or a sample request?

alex_support: Pasting minimal repro (sanitized):

```json
{
  "input": "Get customer subscription details for user id 123",
  "function_call": {
    "name": "get_subscription",
    "arguments": {
      "user_id": 123
    },
    "response_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "plan": {"type": "string"},
        "renewal_date": {"type": "string", "format": "date"},
        "limits": {"type": "object"}
      },
      "required": ["plan","renewal_date"]
    }
  }
}
```

alex_support: Customer trace shows a series of router hops: request -> tool-router v2 -> schema-validator -> function-exec. The schema-validator shows ~700-1200ms on p99 in the trace.

maria_eng-runtime: Interesting. We recently shipped pre-compiled schema support but only for hosted models; tool router still runs a generic JSONSchema.validate call with ajv? I thought we switched to AJV compiled validators last quarter.

sam_platform: We added a compatibility shim last week for deep coercion that falls back to the slower validator when `coerceTypes: true` is on. Could that be triggering heavy paths?

jess_prod: Customer confirmed they enabled strict output validation in their config (validate_output: true) after a recommendation. So they're hitting the validation path.

kevin_oncall: How many concurrent requests are they sending in the repro?

alex_support: They ran 50 concurrent calls in their reproduction, with typical token lengths small (~80 tokens). The p50 is still fine, but p95/p99 blow up.

maria_eng-runtime: That smells like a blocking CPU hotspot in the validator under concurrency. AJV synchronous validation can take time for big nested schemas. Also we do not currently cache compiled validators per schema in the router — we compile per-request when the schema is inline.

ops_bot: deploy_bot reports last change affecting tool-router: 2025-11-12 22:03 UTC — patch added deep-coercion feature to validator.

kevin_oncall: Two action hypotheses: (1) per-request compilation of schema causing CPU latency; (2) validator falls back to slower full-check path when certain schema features used (formats/coercion). Short-term mitigation: disable strict validation for their tenant or route to fallback model without validation. Medium-term: compile schemas once and reuse, or move validation off main request path.

sam_platform: We can add a tenant-scoped in-memory LRU cache keyed by schema fingerprint quickly. Pre-compile AJV validators and store them. That should drop validation time from ~200-800ms to <5ms for compiled validators.

jess_prod: Customer (AcmeCorp) is asking for an immediate mitigation. Can we disable validate_output for their API key server-side as a config toggle?

maria_eng-runtime: Yes — we have a per-tenant routing flag. I can flip `validate_output` to false for AcmeCorp in the runtime config. That would remove the schema-validator hop. Note: this relaxes their enforced schema contract; they requested validation for safety though.

kevin_oncall: Do it as a canary: flip for their API key only and monitor p95/p99. Also increase sampling of schema validation errors in background once disabled so we still collect mismatches.

alex_support: I'll ask customer to accept temporary disable while we fix it.

sam_platform: For a medium-term patch, I'll open a PR to add compiled-validator LRU cache + background validation. Plan: compile inline schemas on first sight, store compiled validator, then run validator on fast path. If compiled validation throws, fall back to full check and log details.

maria_eng-runtime: Also consider offloading validation to a small worker pool so router threads aren't blocked. Worker can validate asynchronously and if validation fails, we can still return a 206/partial result or schedule a retry depending on policy.

kevin_oncall: Good. Another immediate tweak: increase tool-router worker threads on the node pool to reduce queueing. That reduces p99 tail while we patch validator. But watch CPU.

jess_prod: Customer confirmed they need validation on for compliance — can't keep it off for long. Request ETA for compiled validators and worker offload.

sam_platform: Estimate: small PR + canary in staging in ~2 days, prod roll within 1 week if no issues. Worker offload is more invasive — 2–3 weeks.

maria_eng-runtime: For observability, we should add per-schema metrics: compile_time, validate_time histogram, cache_hit_rate, and instrument the tool-router traces to attribute latency to either compile or validate step.

alex_support: I've added these as immediate monitoring requests to the console team. Need per-tenant dashboards and alert when schema validation p95 > 300ms.

ops_bot: alert created: schema-validation-p95 > 300ms for >5m on tenant.* (ID: INC-20251113-42)

kevin_oncall: Action items:
- alex_support: get customer sign-off for temporary disable and sample logs (by end of day)
- maria_eng-runtime: flip tenant flag for AcmeCorp as a canary and monitor (ETA 30m)
- sam_platform: open PR for compiled-validator cache + unit tests (ETA 48h)
- platform infra: scale tool-router pool by +20% for the next 24h (watch CPU)

alex_support: I'll handle comms. Customer is nervous but appreciates quick triage.

maria_eng-runtime: Flip done for AcmeCorp. Early telemetry shows p95 dropped to ~260ms and p99 to ~540ms. Still slightly elevated vs baseline but much better.

kevin_oncall: Keep an eye on error rates — if any schema mismatches start happening we need to capture sample payloads (with PII redacted).

sam_platform: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/validator-cache/pull/87 — includes LRU per-tenant cache, compiled AJV usage, and a toggle to disable coercion fallback to fast path. Requesting review from @maria_eng-runtime and @kevin_oncall.

jess_prod: Great. Please keep me posted; AcmeCorp needs a follow-up timeline for compliance re-enablement.

alex_support: Will do. I'll post updates in this thread and create a short customer-facing summary once we have the fix in prod. :thumbsup:

maria_eng-runtime: Long-term note: consider standardizing schema templates and distributing compiled validators at model onboarding time to avoid inline heavy schemas. Also evaluate replacing AJV with Rust-based validator for router-critical path.

kevin_oncall: Closing loop — mark incident as mitigated for now. We'll track the PR and follow up with a postmortem if rollout goes wrong.

deploy_bot: [deploy] rolled back tool-router feature flag v2-deep-coercion for tenant AcmeCorp at 2025-11-13T03:12:45Z.

alex_support: Thanks team.

maria_eng-runtime: Filing follow-up doc with repro steps and perf numbers (will link here when ready).

alex_support: Thread summary (for notes): 1) Customer p95/p99 regression caused by heavy per-request schema validation for function calling. 2) Short-term: disable validate_output for tenant (canary) + scale tool-router. 3) Medium-term: compiled-validator cache + worker offload + better metrics. 4) Customer updated and mitigating change applied.

kevin_oncall: Nice work.
